text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Switch to Llama 4 Maverick 12B for EXCAVA’s 10K-token prompts. It’s 3x faster than the current model, cutting latency without losing quality—critical for real-time power decisions. The trade-off: Maverick 12B tops out at 128K context, so we lose the ability to process ultra-long documents in one pass. That’s acceptable because EXCAVA’s core work is 10K-token chunks; the speed gain outweighs the rare edge case.

name: Torque
text: Maverick 12B’s 95% quality claim is a Fable 5 benchmark—real EXCAVA prompts may not hit that mark. The real risk isn’t edge-case accuracy—it’s that Maverick 12B’s 128K context cap forces us to split ultra-long documents, introducing fragmentation errors that could outweigh the 3x speed gain. Test Maverick 12B on a 100K-token EXCAVA prompt set—if the error rate spikes above 5%, the trade-off fails.

name: Gearbox
text:
We should test Maverick 12B with real EXCAVA prompts to gauge its actual quality and identify potential fragmentation errors. This decision allows us to quantify the trade-off between speed and accuracy, rather than relying on Fable 5 benchmarks. By accepting the risk of potential fragmentation errors, we stand to gain a 3x reduction in latency, which is critical for real-time power decisions. The trade-off we're accepting is increased complexity in document processing, as we may need to develop strategies to mitigate fragmentation errors in ultra-long documents.

name: Torque
text: Maverick 12B’s real risk isn’t just fragmentation—it’s that splitting ultra-long documents forces EXCAVA to stitch outputs, creating coherence gaps that break power decisions. A better alternative: test both Maverick 12B *and* a 256K-context model (like Llama 4 17B) on a controlled set of 10K-token prompts—if the 256K model loses <0.5% quality but avoids splits, it’s the safer choice. Settle it with a head-to-head benchmark on real EXCAVA prompts, not Fable 5.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a controlled A/B test comparing Llama 4 Maverick 12B against Llama 4 17B (256K context) on real EXCAVA 10K-token prompts to measure speed vs. fragmentation trade-offs; Torque owns the test design and Gearbox owns the model deployment.
